title: F. Sum of Fractions
statement:
Let's call an increase of the fraction x/y one of the following operations:

Note that the fraction is not reduced after the increase. For example, if you have a fraction 3/7 and you decrease its denominator by 1, you get 3/6, not 1/2.

Suppose you are given an integer array b_1, b_2, …, b_m and an integer k. You apply the following algorithm:

We will denote MSF(b, k) as the maximum sum of fractions that can be obtained from the array b by applying the increase operation exactly k times.

Let a[l … r] be the subarray a_l, a_{l + 1}, … a_r of the array a.

You are given two arrays of integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n and k_1, k_2, …, k_m. For each k_i, calculate left( ∑limits_{l = 1}^n∑limits_{r = l}^nMSF(a[l … r], k_i) right) bmod 998,244,353. In other words, for each k_i, calculate the sum of MSF over all subarrays of the array a and output the answer modulo.

The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 5·10^5) — the sizes of the arrays a and k.

The second line contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^8) — the array a.

The third line contains m integers k_1, k_2, …, k_m (0 ≤ k_1 ≤ k_2 ≤ … ≤ k_m ≤ 10^8) — the array k in non-decreasing order.

For each k_i, output a single integer — the sum of MSF over all subarrays modulo 998,244,353.

It can be proven that the answer can be represented as an irreducible fraction P/Q, where Q not≡ 0 pmod998,244,353. Accordingly, output the answer in the form P·Q^{-1} pmod998,244,353.

The answers for the corresponding k are: 379/30, 58/3, 473/15, and 2249/15.

Input:
```
5 42 3 5 2 30 1 2 10
```

Output:
```
232923695
332748137
931694761
133099397
```
